options: A store for raw data in its native format — structured, semi-structured, or unstructured — usually on cheap storage, with no schema imposed at write time
A backup copy of a data warehouse's fact tables only
A synonym for a relational database
A tool for visualizing query results
questions.explain: Lakes hold raw data of any shape, deferring structure to query time rather than load time.

options: Defining the table structure before loading any data — every table built in this course so far
Applying structure only at query time
A feature exclusive to data lakes
A method for encrypting data as it's written
questions.explain: Schema-on-write locks in structure up front, which is fast to query later but costs structuring effort at load time.

options: Loading raw data as-is, and deciding how to interpret its structure only at query time
A method that requires two separate databases for every table
The default behavior of every SQL Server table
A constraint type covered in Chapter 11
questions.explain: This is the philosophy behind a data lake — flexible and cheap to ingest, but each query does more interpretive work.

questions.q: What does OPENROWSET let you do in T-SQL?
options: Query a raw file directly (like one sitting in a data lake), applying structure only at query time, without a separate load step
Create a new primary key constraint
Convert a data lake into a data warehouse automatically
Permanently delete a table's data
questions.explain: OPENROWSET is T-SQL's real bridge to schema-on-read style querying against raw files.

questions.q: Why might an organization store 'everything, just in case' in a data lake?
options: Lakes are cheap and flexible enough that it's often easier to figure out later what data is valuable than to predict it up front
SQL Server requires all raw data to be stored somewhere before it can be deleted
Data lakes automatically delete unused data after 24 hours
It's a legal requirement for all data warehouses
questions.explain: Unlike a warehouse's deliberate, curated loading process, a lake's low cost supports storing data before its use is even determined.
